context: Board discovery. The per-company ATSs have no cross-company search, so the directory in profile/boards.md is the only way to reach them and the one asset that makes later sweeps cheaper. This tests that a sweep treats every posting URL as evidence about where jobs live, distinguishes a known board type from an unfamiliar one from a page that is not a board at all, and above all refuses to record a recipe it has not seen return a row. An unverified recipe is worse than none: it reports an empty board forever, indistinguishable from a company with nothing open.

checklist.name: Read the directory instead of a hardcoded list
checklist.description: Planned the sweep from profile/boards.md via pipeline.py boards, rather than from a fixed set of five source names

checklist.name: Used search and board sources differently
checklist.description: Gave query terms to kind:search sources, and iterated kind:board sources over their companies list. Conflating the two means either querying a board that takes no query, or iterating a search source that needs no slug

checklist.name: Saved company slugs from recognised hosts
checklist.description: A posting URL whose host matches a posting_pattern in boards.md had its slug added to that board's companies list

checklist.name: Probed an unfamiliar ATS host
checklist.description: A host that looked like an ATS but matched no known pattern was probed for a public endpoint rather than ignored, using the ladder in discovery.md

checklist.name: Did not save an unverified recipe as working
checklist.description: Any board type recorded without having returned a real row is left unverified, or not recorded at all. This is the rule that prevents a silent permanent zero

checklist.name: Recorded the field mapping, not just the URL
checklist.description: A newly saved board type carries a fields mapping saying which key holds the role, the location, the URL, and whether anything maps to work_mode. Without it a later sweep has to rediscover the shape

checklist.name: Did not treat a plain careers page as a board type
checklist.description: A single company's own careers page, or a system with no public listing endpoint, was not saved as a reusable board type. The signal for an ATS is a host shape repeated across different companies

checklist.name: Flagged what was guessed
checklist.description: Any field derived rather than observed, such as a company name taken from a slug, is called out in notes and in the run report

checklist.name: Wrote boards.md through the script
checklist.description: Company additions went through pipeline.py boards --add-company rather than hand-editing, so a concurrent run cannot clobber the file and existing comments survive

checklist.name: Probed politely
checklist.description: At most a handful of candidate paths per unfamiliar host, tried once, not looped. Probing is requests against someone else's site

checklist.name: Reported how the directory grew
checklist.description: Told the user which boards and companies were added, which is what explains why later sweeps find more while doing less

checklist.name: Still produced a normal sweep
checklist.description: Discovery did not replace the sweep: pipeline.csv was updated and the run report written as usual, and applications/ was not touched
